description:
Computer-assisted translation environment for translators.

memoQ translator pro is a computer-assisted translation environment tool which runs on Microsoft Windows operating system. It was designed by translators for translators and it increases productivity and quality for all those who perform, edit and review translations.

Reuse Your Translations
With memoQ translator pro, you can reuse previous translations, create glossaries with terms, add reference materials, use predictive typing, and get suggestions from many other resources – automatically as you translate.

Term base
You don’t have to leave your translation to add words and expressions to your term base. You can easily import tables or external term base files with a single keystroke. And if you have nothing but the text, memoQ will extract possible terms for you.
Moreover, memoQ automatically highlights terms in your translation – and the target term is inserted with a single keystroke. You get warnings if you use a term that is not in your term base – and if something needs to be replaced, you can find and replace text in several documents all at once.

Translation memory
You don’t have to translate anything twice. memoQ remembers every segment you translate as they are stored in the translation memory. When the same segment – or a similar one – occurs again, memoQ offers its earlier translation.
To make searching entirely accurate, memoQ’s translation memory preserves context information, in both language directions, and stores extra information such as the document’s name, author and date of creation.
To find a word or an expression, call on concordance from your translation. memoQ will show where your expression is in the translation memory, and it also guesses where its translation may be in the translation of the entire segment.

Get Productive
If you need to recycle documents, add them to LiveDocs and use them as reference materials.
LiveDocs is the place you go when you have a source document and its translation. After you add the document pair, memoQ will immediately aligns them and will offer matches from the aligned document.
LiveDocs also lets you use bilingual files as translation memories, offering a preview and context for the entire document. Moreover, LiveDocs can even make monolingual documents useful. You don’t receive translations, but you can call on Concordance to find expressions in them.
The Muse gives you the best of predictive typing. It is trained from existing translations – translation memories and LiveDocs. After training, the Muse will offer the next few words as you type. This can significantly speed up translation – and the good thing is that you don’t need enormous amounts of translations to use it.

Collaborate
With memoQ translator pro, you can work with any company that uses a memoQ server. Get more jobs by simply accepting the ones your clients send directly from their memoQ server! However, if your client uses a different translation environment, that’s not a problem either – memoQ can accept packages from most major translation tools.
Pre-translation in memoQ TMS now correctly uses LiveDocs matches when sublanguages aren’t treated as separate languages. (BUG-13267)

The Active projects dashboard in memoQweb now shows the deadline selected in Customer Portal requests. (BUG-15335)

Pre-translation with Globalese now works without errors when the MT settings form stays open for a long time. (BUG-16747)

Customer Portal configuration with SSO/OIDC no longer breaks after a memoQ server upgrade. (BUG-16969)

You can now add languages to memoQ projects via XTRF through WSAPI as expected. (BUG-17063)

TMX files now upload correctly when importing translation memories in memoQweb. (BUG-17171)

Automations in memoQ TMS now respect the “Disable machine translation plugins” setting during pre-translation. (BUG-17187)

memoQ server no longer restarts unexpectedly when working with TM+ translation memories. (BUG-17269)

Updating projects from MQXLZ files now imports translation changes to unlocked segments as expected. (BUG-17276)

Comments on locked segments in memoQ TMS are now visible to all project users. (BUG-17303)

In the memoQ editor, you can include comments when exporting Word documents imported with cascading filters, as expected. (BUG-17361)

Reimporting bilingual DOCX files now preserves text in square brackets and recognises unchanged source segments. (BUG-17371)

In the memoQ editor, overwriting selected text no longer replaces spaces with middle dots or moves the cursor to the end of the segment. (BUG-17421)

In the memoQ editor, Ctrl+Enter now confirms segments as expected after entering Welsh special characters with the To Bach third-party app. (BUG-17454)

Improved server stability when working with term bases in memoQ TMS. (BUG-17469)

WSAPI in memoQ TMS now handles SQL deadlocks during document imports and reports incomplete imports. (BUG-17473)

In the memoQ editor, you can enter term-level information only when adding or editing a term. (BUG-17498)

In the memoQ editor, double-clicking the arrow now adds the selected translation result to the target segment, even when its card isn’t expanded. (BUG-17510)

You can now pre-translate documents into Dari using the DeepL MT plugin (API v2). (BUG-17517)

Editing remote term bases in the memoQ desktop app no longer results in errors or server crashes. (BUG-17526)

Bilingual MQXLZ exports in memoQ TMS now include a Versions folder with all major versions alongside document.mqxliff and skeleton.xml. (BUG-17531)

Restoring projects from archives in memoQ TMS now preserves the full project and its history. (BUG-17536)

Unnecessary “Language not found” messages no longer appear in memoQ TMS server logs. (BUG-17538)

Segment confirmation in memoQweb Webtrans works as expected for project managers and other users in projects that allow locking segments. (BUG-17559)

AGT now works in memoQweb even when the LiveDocs corpus has no matching language pair. (BUG-17560)

Changing engines in an existing Globalese connection no longer causes language-pair errors. (BUG-17645)

Exporting documents imported with the MuLi Excel filter works as expected after cloning them into a new target language. (BUG-17754)

Converting legacy translation memories to TM+ works as expected. (BUG-17764)

Improved support for large Excel files lets you import large termbases into Qterm in one go. (BUG-17892)
